text: {"findings":[{"rule":"K2","where":"ClaimIssuer.revokeClaim / ClaimIssuer.isClaimValid / ClaimIssuer.revokedClaims, reached through Identity.addClaim and IdentityRegistry.isVerified","severity":"HIGH","why":"Revocation is keyed on the raw signature bytes, but ECDSA signatures are malleable. The investor can flip s to n-s and flip v, which gives a different byte string that still recovers to the same issuer signer. The revoked claim can then be re-added and still passes isVerified, so a revoked wallet can receive tokens again.","steps":"1) Issuer admin calls claimIssuer.revokeClaim(claimId, idA), which stores revokedClaims[sig]=true. 2) Investor a1 reads the original sig (r,s,v) from idA.getClaim(claimId). 3) a1 computes s' = n - s and v' = v XOR 1 (27<->28) and calls idA.addClaim(1, 1, claimIssuer, r||s'||v', data, \"\"). The validity check passes because the new bytes are not in revokedClaims and recover to the same signer. 4) a1 (or a2, same identity) calls token.transfer(x, amount) to a verified receiver, and it succeeds."}]}
